root_cause.text: In `vgic_its_invalidate_cache()`, the function calls `vgic_put_irq()` on the iterated pointer from `xa_for_each()` instead of on the value returned by `xa_erase()`, enabling concurrent invocations from different locking contexts to drop the same cache entry's reference multiple times and cause a use-after-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx); vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);` with `irq = xa_erase(&its->translation_cache, idx); if (irq) vgic_put_irq(kvm, irq);`. The commit message explains: "It puts the iterated pointer, though, rather than the value returned by xa_erase()" and "Two or more of them can drain the same cache concurrently, and if each one observes the same entry, erases it and then puts it, the single reference the cache holds on that entry is dropped more than once."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add null check after xa_erase in vgic_its_invalidate_cache to ensure vgic_put_irq is only called when an entry was actually erased.
intent_record.what: In the loop over translation_cache entries, replaced unconditional xa_erase and vgic_put_irq with assigning the result of xa_erase to irq and then calling vgic_put_irq only if irq is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: Previously, vgic_put_irq was called for every entry returned by xa_for_each, even if xa_erase had already removed it (returning NULL). Now vgic_put_irq is only called when xa_erase actually erases an entry, preventing double-unref or invocation on NULL.
